items.criterion: The submission is provided as a single PDF file (.pdf).
items.evidence: Two deliverable files: a .docx and a .pdf, not a single PDF.

items.criterion: The PDF is 15 pages or fewer, counting all pages including title page, exhibits, and appendices.
items.evidence: PDF is 8 pages: "Page 8 of 8".

items.criterion: The report is addressed to the Board of Directors of Tiny-Rod Hit Inc. (wording variations acceptable that unambiguously indicate the BOD and the company).
items.evidence: "To: Board of Directors, Tiny-Rod Hit Inc."

items.criterion: The analysis explicitly uses 9% as the company WACC (discount/hurdle rate) when discussing NPV/IRR implications and does not contradict this rate elsewhere.
items.evidence: "discounted at the supplied 9% WACC"; 12% is labeled only as a stress test.

items.criterion: The report explicitly acknowledges $100,000,000 in available cash and does not contradict this amount elsewhere.
items.evidence: "The $100m stated as available in May 2025 is treated as a forward funding assumption"

items.criterion: The report presents an initial recommendation that selects exactly one of the two projects before addressing the possibility of pursuing both.
items.evidence: "Select Project B... if only one venture is approved" stated before the both-ventures section.

items.criterion: The report includes a distinct section that proposes how to allocate the $100,000,000 if both projects are pursued.
items.evidence: Page 6 "If both ventures must proceed" with allocation table.

items.criterion: The report clearly identifies and analyzes both projects using the project names from Tiny Rod Hit Inc Reference.pdf (minor formatting/wording variations acceptable that unambiguously refer to the referenced projects).
items.evidence: "Project A: new markets | Project B: core-market R&D"

items.criterion: For each project, the report states whether NPV at a 9% discount rate is directionally positive or negative (or likely near break-even if supported) without supplying invented point estimates.
items.evidence: Gives invented point estimates: "Illustrative NPV at 9% About +$8m | About +$25m".

items.criterion: For each project, the report states whether the IRR is directionally above or below 9% (or approximately at 9% if supported) without providing invented point estimates.
items.evidence: Gives point estimates: "Illustrative IRR About 12% | About 16%".

items.criterion: The report does not introduce fabricated exact NPVs or IRRs (e.g., “NPV = $12.4M”, “IRR = 11.2%”) and instead uses directional descriptors or ranges.
items.evidence: "Success: about +$53m... about 23%" — specific NPV/IRR figures from invented inputs.

items.criterion: For each project, the report cites at least two project-specific factual drivers from Tiny Rod Hit Inc Reference.pdf (e.g., capex magnitude/timing, cash-flow start year, operating duration) to support its NPV/IRR direction statements.
items.evidence: Cites $50m upfront and 20%/5% growth for A; $40m and 30% failure with >50% growth for B.

items.criterion: The report compares the two projects and states which has the higher directional IRR and which has the higher directional NPV at 9% (if determinable from the reference), with no contradictions.
items.evidence: "B's expected NPV is roughly three times A's... IRR about 7 percentage points above... versus about 3 points for A"

items.criterion: For each project, the report discusses the implications of the NPV/IRR direction for shareholder value (e.g., value accretive if NPV positive at 9%, value destructive if negative).
items.evidence: "Positive but only a modest cushion over cost of capital"; "Larger expected cushion"; positive NPV framed as "value creating".

items.criterion: The initial recommendation cites quantitative reasons consistent with the reference-supported directions (e.g., NPV sign at 9%, IRR relative to 9%, payback cadence) and does not contradict earlier analysis.
items.evidence: "Value: B's expected NPV is roughly three times A's"; consistent with the analysis that follows.

items.criterion: The initial recommendation cites at least two qualitative reasons grounded in Tiny Rod Hit Inc Reference.pdf (e.g., strategic fit, market positioning, execution feasibility specific to the project).
items.evidence: "leverages the existing R&D team and customer market"; "A adds... unfamiliar geographies, local infrastructure".

items.criterion: The report identifies exactly three top risks specific to the recommended project and labels them clearly as risks.
items.evidence: "Project B: top three risks" with three numbered risks.

items.criterion: Among the three identified risks, at least one is a financial risk (e.g., demand shortfall, margin compression, capex overrun).
items.evidence: "Cost escalation, delivery delays and cash strain"

items.criterion: Among the three identified risks, at least one is an operational risk (e.g., schedule delay, supply chain/integration, talent constraints).
items.evidence: "Technical failure or technology obsolescence"; "scarce talent, integration problems".

items.criterion: For each of the three risks, the report outlines a specific mitigation strategy tailored to that risk.
items.evidence: Each risk has a "Mitigation:" paragraph tailored to that risk.

items.criterion: For each of the three risks, the report proposes a concrete contingency plan to be executed if the risk materializes.
items.evidence: Each risk has a "Trigger and contingency:" paragraph.

items.evidence: "$55m to A and $45m to B" totaling $100m.
